knowledge:
- key_parameters: spikeslab=logical determining whether to use a sparsity-promoting spike-and-slab prior (defaults to TRUE) ;; factoriseQ=logical determining whether to use a fully-factorised mean-field variational approximation (defaults to TRUE) ;; n_rep=integer specifying the number of random initializations to train multiple models and select the one with the highest ELBO ;; th=numeric threshold on the ELBO change for convergence in the variational Bayes algorithm ;; family=character string specifying the response distribution, such as "binomial" for logistic regression ;; calcELB=logical indicating whether to calculate the evidence lower bound (must be set to FALSE for logistic regression)
- alternatives: none mentioned
- when_to_use: Use when performing regression or classification on high-dimensional datasets where features are naturally grouped (e.g., multi-omics data) and different groups are expected to have different relative strengths of penalization and sparsity.
- pitfalls: The logistic regression implementation is experimental, not optimized for speed, and can be slow on large datasets ;; The evidence lower bound (ELBO) is not calculated for logistic regression, meaning convergence cannot be monitored and the algorithm will only stop when the maximum number of iterations is reached ;; Variational Bayes posterior distributions are often too concentrated and should not be used directly for constructing confidence intervals, though they provide good point estimates.

workflows.name: linear_regression
workflows.intent: Fit a group-penalized linear regression model on high-dimensional continuous data, evaluate convergence, extract coefficients, and make predictions.
workflows.stages: 1. Fit the linear regression model using graper ;; 2. Plot the ELBO to monitor convergence using plotELBO ;; 3. Plot posterior distributions of parameters using plotPosterior ;; 4. Extract coefficients and intercept using coef ;; 5. Extract posterior inclusion probabilities using getPIPs ;; 6. Plot group-wise penalties using plotGroupPenalties ;; 7. Predict response on new data using predict
workflows.code:
fit <- graper(Xtrain, ytrain, annot, n_rep=3, verbose=FALSE, th=0.001)
plotELBO(fit)
plotPosterior(fit, "gamma", gamma0=data$gammas, range=c(0, 20))
plotPosterior(fit, "pi", pi0=data$pis)
beta <- coef(fit, include_intercept=FALSE)
intercept <- fit$intercept
pips <- getPIPs(fit)
plotGroupPenalties(fit)
preds <- predict(fit, Xtest)

workflows.name: logistic_regression
workflows.intent: Fit a group-penalized logistic regression model on high-dimensional binary data, extract coefficients, and make predictions.
workflows.stages: 1. Fit the logistic regression model using graper with family="binomial" and calcELB=FALSE ;; 2. Plot posterior distributions of parameters using plotPosterior ;; 3. Extract coefficients and intercept using coef ;; 4. Extract posterior inclusion probabilities using getPIPs ;; 5. Predict response on new data using predict
workflows.code:
fit <- graper(Xtrain, ytrain, annot, verbose=FALSE, family="binomial", calcELB=FALSE)
plotPosterior(fit, "gamma", gamma0=data$gammas)
plotPosterior(fit, "pi", pi0=data$pis)
beta <- coef(fit, include_intercept=FALSE)
intercept <- fit$intercept
pips <- getPIPs(fit)
preds <- predict(fit, Xtest)
